# Offline harness and tool policy construction

Status: Offline construction verified (2026-10-01). Final lint and all 297 default tests pass after the approved request identity clarification. DSR-1.1 and DSR-1.2 remain IN PROGRESS because this bounded construction does not close their remaining acceptance and dependency gates. No paid model call, contact, commit or push occurred.

## Authority and boundaries

The operator approved the limited continuity recorded in [DSR-0.2](../decisions/DSR-0.2-v1-scope.md#offline-implementation-continuity-approval). This permits offline construction for DSR-1.1 and DSR-1.2 before budget and contact blockers close. It does not satisfy the real model proofs, retire engine assumptions or open Phase 2.

The execution repository is `<repo>`, based on `69f5497d3d3dec7ad3269c72ff266c2931c9f379`. The approved lock repair is retained separately as described in [the baseline setup record](2026-09-30-baseline-setup.md). Installed versions remain Python 3.13.15, Temporal SDK 1.33.0 and Claude Agent SDK 0.2.154. After construction verification, the operator authorized commits: dependency repair `d70ce0b13a3b3eca07707ccc88c8a9494bd58032` and implementation `99fb461a074debfcaff6308cb0a3454b93991ed2`, followed by a push to the fork's `design-base` branch. The [commit checkpoint record](2026-10-01-commit-checkpoint.md) owns their exact tree identities, fresh per commit checks, verified remote tip, and remaining CI limits. No pull request or hosted CI success is claimed.

## Construction

The offline helper drives the production runner through a scoped simulated SDK stream. Explicit configuration includes an engine path, model, credential reference, spend cap and token threshold. Provider execution always refuses. Records label engine version, usage and transcript as simulated; checkpoint storage is mocked. Observed token counts do not prevent a call from exceeding a token limit. A process lock rejects overlapping helper runs before their SDK patches can interfere.

The opt in policy carries exact retained tool names and immutable classifications. Unknown names and author MCP tools have no authority. The hook defers effects and questions and performs basic read path checks. An identical paused request can defer again; every different call after pause and every call after stop is denied. The private slot binds ID, name and canonical JSON inputs, and the runner compares the returned deferred request before checkpointing. [The approved decision](../decisions/DSR-1.2-hook-request-identity.md) owns the official citation, engineering reasoning and remaining cross segment binding gap. Skill stays denied until validated package configuration exists. Full read confinement, real engine interception and process isolation are not implemented by this change.

Policy options admit only a string `system_prompt` and an empty `extra_args` mapping. Each has a reason in the product README. Options are copied before use, effect tools are omitted from automatic approvals, permission mode is `default`, and the permission callback only denies. Legacy mode remains the default. A deferred policy effect or question retains the blocked call and refuses another segment because the executor and signed question handler do not exist yet.

## Review and verification ledger

- Initial harness selection: 22 passed.
- Initial combined selection: 98 passed.
- Expanded runner detector, input mutation and harness overlap selection: 107 passed. No live provider stream ran.
- Independent review found duration serialization failure at the Temporal Activity boundary and a retry path that could discard effect observations. Both are fixed. The policy travels as canonical JSON text and reconstructs all five duration fields; converter round trips cover each. Observations are collected before cleanup and take precedence over retryable stream and store errors. Fresh focused review confirmed these fixes and cancellation propagation.
- The 224 case full regression run passed before the final conservative error wording correction. After the correction, all 121 new offline cases passed, followed by the exact final full run: `225 passed` in 200.67 seconds. Parsed `junit/offline-policy.xml` contains 104 legacy cases and 121 new cases, with zero failures, errors or skips. Report SHA-256: `1bd69f829058b94d2df804a6c5b31399fcf8da444b08f7540288f990809d86e7`. The baseline report is preserved separately. Logs include fake API broken pipe and local server warnings; the suite and XML checks pass. Verification is Linux with Python 3.13.15 only, not the complete CI platform matrix.
- Final `make lint`: PASS for 52 files, including Ruff, Pyright, Mypy, Basedpyright and Pydocstyle. Pyright printed an available version notice; no tool version was changed.
- The approved lock hash remains `6a44031e205f0c7e356ab6bb24d85166554dedca9f3084e710c6c1dec51260b6`. `git diff --check` passes. The tracked added lines and new files were checked for workspace identifiers, local operator paths and internal ticket IDs, with no matches.
- Ticket structure gate: PASS, 67 blocks.
- Plan evidence gate after clarification: PASS, 90 evidence rows and 56 assumptions.
- Current spec evidence gate after clarification: FAIL because it now requires `## Decisions <owner> must make`, which this spec lacks. Its schema, 130 evidence rows, seven invariants, 56 assumptions and source resolution checks pass. This preexisting document compatibility issue is not fixed by changing the gate or inventing owner decisions during offline implementation.

## Approved hook clarification verification

The clarification adds 45 decision table cases and 27 request identity and malformed input cases. Independent review found an uncaught recursion failure that could replace cancellation while reading a deeply nested marker. The fix normalizes excessive JSON nesting into validation failures, places policy UTF8 decoding inside validation, and preserves cancellation. Fresh focused review found no remaining material defect in this change. Legacy parsing and plain ID marker behavior remain separate and unchanged.

Required `make format`, `make sync` and `make lint` pass. The targeted policy and offline harness selection passes all 193 cases. The final full command is `make test PYTEST_ARGS='-s --junit-xml=junit/hook-identity.xml'`: 297 passed in 213.51 seconds. Parsed XML contains 104 legacy cases, 170 policy cases and 23 offline harness cases, with zero failures, errors or skips. Report SHA-256: `d37f56fc4e97b3967f2cd5fbe633b33fa4a688e4f28812977c726f89d967299f`. The previous 225 case report and lock hashes remain unchanged. `git diff --check` and the boundary identifier sweeps pass. The suite prints 30 no credential warnings plus local test server and fake API warnings; no paid provider call ran.

Identity tests include `test_paused_identity_rejects_reused_id_with_changed_request`, `test_paused_identity_accepts_equivalent_nested_object_order`, `test_concurrent_different_policy_requests_have_only_one_winner`, `test_runner_matches_returned_deferred_request_before_checkpoint`, and `test_deep_marker_does_not_replace_runner_cancellation`. Concurrency evidence uses threads and a local filesystem, not distributed filesystem visibility or a real engine batch. Verification remains Linux/Python 3.13.15 only.

## Remaining acceptance work

DSR-1.1 remains incomplete: real model runs, measured budget stopping, a selected newest engine lane, actual full transcripts and credential scrubbing of real records are not proved. [Minimum engine preparation](2026-10-01-minimum-engine-environment.md) now records wheel 0.2.153 and engine 2.1.273, alongside the repaired baseline rather than a newest lane. No minimum lane plugin compatibility suite ran. The helper contains no path that enables paid execution.

DSR-1.2 has verified offline construction, including the approved decision table clarification, request identity checks, reviewed fixes, final lint and full legacy regression. Its corrected decision table criterion is checked with named test evidence; this is not unconditional read admission or real engine interception proof. Skill remains intentionally denied pending its validator. Already answered IDs still lack durable name and input binding across segments. Contact is still deferred. Engine batching, permission precedence and real model defer and resume require the later proof tickets. No safe Bash recovery, effect executor, signed question handler or Phase 1 exit is claimed.
